Illegal tyre waste operation company and director ordered to pay £69k by courts

14 October 2025

A company and its director have been ordered to pay a total of £69,000 after running an illegal tyre waste operation in Powys.

Benji and Co Limited, a tyre recycling business based in Welshpool, and its director Peter Rees, 52, of Newtown, appeared at Swansea Crown Court on 14 October 2025.

The court heard that between 2021 and 2023, the company had been accepting waste tyres at a site without the required environmental permit. Over 50,000 waste tyres were found stockpiled at the site when NRW officers conducted an inspection in March 2023.

The company had previously been warned about the need for an environmental permit in 2020, but continued to operate illegally.

Benji and Co Limited pleaded guilty to two charges: operating a regulated facility without an environmental permit contrary to Regulation 12 of the Environmental Permitting Regulations 2016, and failing to comply with a notice contrary to Section 34 of the Environmental Protection Act 1990.

Peter Rees pleaded guilty to knowingly permitting the company to operate without a permit, contrary to Section 33 of the Environmental Protection Act 1990.

Her Honour Judge Catherine Phillips said: "This was a sustained and deliberate breach of environmental law motivated by profit. The company saved significant sums by avoiding the costs of proper waste management."

Benji and Co Limited was fined £40,000 and ordered to pay £15,000 in prosecution costs. Peter Rees was fined £10,000. Both were required to pay a £2,000 victim surcharge each.

The total penalties amount to £69,000.

NRW's Regulatory Manager for Mid Wales said: "We will always pursue those who flout environmental regulations and seek to profit from illegal waste activities. This case sends a clear message that such behaviour will not be tolerated."

The company has been ordered to clear the site of all waste tyres within six months.
